course: 1C:Enterprise 8 Programming — from foundations to professional development
module: Platform architecture, infobases and development environments
title: Developer tools: diagnose an error and preserve a clear change
goal: Diagnose your own error, preserve a working version and distinguish tool purposes.

prerequisites.text: Distinguish saving source, updating the database configuration and execution.

sections.title: A development environment is not the runtime
paragraphs: Designer ships with the platform and is the reproducible P1 path. EDT is a separate Eclipse-based environment supporting projects and Git. It can target different platform versions and infobases, but running an application still requires the platform. Having an EDT project does not establish successful application to an infobase.

At the audit date the official website offers EDT 2026.2.2. We do not claim it is installed or tested with our workspace. Redistribution rights cannot be inferred from Eclipse licensing; the product and components need a separate check. Designer is sufficient for P1; EDT remains an optional additional validation path.

Designer from the official installation is sufficient for the first lessons. Do not install several editors for one message. EDT is a separate development environment useful for larger projects. BSL Language Server analyzes source statically. Git tracks source history. Their jobs differ: neither a commit history nor colored syntax proves application execution.

sections.title: A missing quote
paragraphs: The opening quote has no closing partner. Restore it before the closing parenthesis.

code.output: The check rejects the unfinished string; execution is not claimed.

tables.caption: Step-by-step reasoning
rows: Correct the source line and check again.

sections.title: Highlighting, BSL LS and OneScript
paragraphs: BSL Language Server supplies analysis and editor capabilities. Its LGPL license and diagnostics do not turn it into a 1C engine. The candidate does not integrate it and therefore makes no BSL LS static PASS claim. Native configuration checking is a separate executed mechanism with a version and negative control.

OneScript uses MPL-2.0 and executes an independent language implementation. It may support bounded language exercises but cannot stand in for 1C forms or registers. Neither OneScript nor BSL LS is added to mandatory Nexus startup. A provider/bridge decision needs 02/01 coordination and a threat model rather than a catalog flag change.

Read a diagnostic as an investigation coordinate: module or file, line and what was expected instead of the observed symbol. A missing quote can produce a message on the following line even though the cause is above. Compare the changed line with the last working one, correct one cause and repeat the check. Do not erase the handler merely to suppress diagnostics.

sections.title: Git preserves an explainable change
paragraphs: A commit should connect the problem, change and verification. Preserve sources, a concise protocol and safe evidence. Exclude working infobases, licensing files, personal connection parameters and installers. Reviewers need to see the changed module and the test expectations justifying it. Project commit messages are in Russian.

Avoid diverging copies of shared definitions. The course glossary is versioned and referenced by lessons, while learning results remain course-specific. A future shared-content update must not silently reinterpret a saved attempt; it needs a new version and compatibility review.

Preserve a working version before editing. A separate source-text file and change note suffice for the first small program. Git adds comparable history: change, reason and validation. Keep licenses, passwords, third-party infobases and real personal data out of source and commits. A source copy is not a .dt data backup.

sections.title: A meaning error with valid syntax
paragraphs: A syntax analyzer does not know the intended sum; compare the requirement and result.

tables.caption: Step-by-step reasoning
rows: Change the operator and execute again.

sections.title: Diagnose from observation to hypothesis
paragraphs: When output is absent, first identify the completed stage: creation, loading, checking, update or execution. Then compare version, directory and source hash. File-access failure does not prove missing licensing; syntax failure does not prove a broken platform. State a narrow hypothesis that one safe experiment can falsify.

During author verification, access to a new infobase file was initially denied by the execution environment. The same operation on that same isolated workspace succeeded with permitted local access. We preserved the failed attempt and explanation without inventing a platform defect or touching production. Record problem → hypothesis → attempt → result → decision → regression.

Separate diagnostics before execution from result checking after it. Syntactically valid “30 - 45” is still wrong when a sum is required. Later tests will fix expected values; now repeat the known message and explain the observation’s scope. A disappeared error marker indicates corrected diagnostics, not automatic practice credit.

sections.title: Check your explanation
paragraphs: Syntax color means the program is correct. Highlighting, analysis and execution serve different purposes.
Git will restore every customer. Source history is not an infobase data backup.

practice.title: Correct your own error and repeat validation
practice.task: Record one change: what, why, validation and return path.
practice.environment: Your training infobase and a preserved working source copy.
practice.externalRoute: Designer of your own infobase; EDT, Git and BSL LS are optional introductions

steps.title: Preserve working source
steps.action: Copy only your short handler into a separate text file with a clear name. Record its previously working message.
steps.why: A negative experiment needs a return path.
steps.expected: The working source is available separately.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not export third-party modules or registration details.
steps.before: The preceding startup message has run; its working source is preserved separately.

steps.title: Obtain a meaningful diagnostic
steps.where: The same module in your own training copy
steps.action: Temporarily remove the closing quote from the message. Run Designer’s syntax check and read the indicated module and line. Do not launch the rejected version.
steps.why: Verify that the changed text is actually analyzed.
steps.expected: The error is found; the saved working copy is intact.
steps.troubleshooting: For a diagnostic on the next line, inspect an unfinished construct above.
steps.before: The working source is available separately.

steps.title: Restore and check
steps.action: Restore the closing quote and compare with the preserved line. Repeat the check and wait for completion.
steps.why: Repair the cause instead of hiding the code.
steps.expected: The same check no longer reports this error.
steps.troubleshooting: Correct remaining errors individually; do not substitute an empty module.
steps.before: The error is found; the saved working copy is intact.

steps.title: Repeat native execution
steps.action: Save, update your infobase and start the application. Compare the message with the last successful version. Separately record checking and execution.
steps.why: Valid syntax and required behavior are separate conditions.
steps.troubleshooting: For old text verify the infobase and update; do not delete other projects.
steps.before: The same check no longer reports this error.

criteria: Identify module, line and correction; preserve the main working source.
Check/analyzer; source history; native platform execution.
Exact edit and observed result; no secrets or data-backup claim based only on .bsl.
Working source before and after correction.
A diagnostic without personal information and the actual new launch message.
The syntax check must reject an unterminated string. Missing expected output after repair leaves the practice incomplete.
